Subject: Merchant commission VAT: responsibility and invoice reissue

Hi Nina / Paul,

Following our recent onboarding call, attached is a pro-forma for the first settlement (RDW-2026-457). Meridian's contract references a standard merchant commission and specifies that VAT treatment follows the place-of-supply rules for B2B services. Before we issue the live invoice we need to confirm two things:

1) Which Meridian entity will be the billed legal entity for June settlement (EU VAT vs non-EU).
2) Whether Meridian will provide a valid EU VAT ID that allows us to apply reverse-charge (zero-rated on our side).

If you can confirm the EU VAT number for the billed entity (or confirm reverse-charge applies), we will reissue the invoice accordingly. I attached a copy of the Proforma and left the payment terms as NET 30 for now.

Attachments: Proforma_Invoice_RDW-457.pdf

Next steps suggested:
- If you confirm an EU VAT ID, we will reissue the invoice with reverse-charge wording and no VAT applied.
- If not, we'll need to apply the appropriate VAT/GST and discuss netting options for merchant commissions.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Ben Carter

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the pro-forma. Meridian will be billed to MeridianTech EU Ltd (registered in IE). Our VAT ID for that entity is IE1234567AB. I've attached the VAT certificate for quick reference.

We typically expect vendors to apply reverse-charge when the supplier is outside the EU and the customer is an EU VAT-registered business. Does Redwood need any additional documentation to support the reverse-charge on your accounting side? Also note: our settlements team requires a brief note on the invoice stating "reverse charge - VAT to be accounted for by the recipient" for internal processing.

Regards,

Paul Thompson
Head of Finance Ops | MeridianTech
